closing.note: SC deed recording fee is $1.85 per $500 of consideration, split state/county. Buyer closing costs typically 2–4% of purchase price.

tax.note: Annual tax ≈ market value × 4% × (millage in mills / 1000). Owner-occupied is exempt from school operating millage per Act 388; primary classification deadline is Jan 15 the tax year after purchase.
tax.typical_owner_millage_note: ESTIMATE — combined county+district+fire+other for unincorporated Spartanburg County; verify with the County Auditor for the exact TMS.

user.deal_breakers: HOA > $100/mo, flood zone, septic, >20 min commute
user.must_haves: 3 bed / 3 bath, 1400+ sqft, 2-car garage, fiber, dedicated 20A

caveats: Percentiles are the value. FEMA's five rating labels are binned separately per hazard, so the same label means different things for different hazards.
A hazard with no rating is not modeled for that tract. That is unknown, not low risk.
The per-ZIP figure is the single census tract containing the ZIP centroid. It is a sample of the ZIP, not an average over it.
Community resilience is published per county and joined onto the tract table, so it does not vary between tracts within the county.
Nothing on this page scores hazard risk. It is reported as a caveat, the same treatment a pre-2000 build year gets.

submarkets.invalidation: Buy here only if you value walkability over land + schools — city price weakness combined with a soft market means longer time-to-appreciation.
submarkets.name: Downtown / City of Spartanburg
notes: $247K–$267K city medians, weakest YoY of the metro (SAR city LMU June 2026: −7.5%).
Walkable inventory, older housing stock; some new townhome projects rezoned 2026.
Best if you want short commute + downtown amenities and can tolerate higher crime and property-tax base.

submarkets.invalidation: Traffic on US-9/Boiling Springs Rd during BMW shift changes; verify actual commute for your work hours, not just the isochrone average.
submarkets.name: Boiling Springs
notes: Fastest-growing suburb north of the city; DR Horton Baxter Village (167 acres, Hwy 9) breaking ground.
Listing count actually shrinking YoY (−17%) — supply tightening while other suburbs pile up.
Fiber coverage strong (~50%) vs. metro peers; solid pick for homelab.

submarkets.invalidation: 22-minute commute is at your 20-min deal-breaker edge. Skip unless you also value the acreage that Inman uniquely offers.
submarkets.name: Inman
notes: Multi-family community + new industrial park breaking ground in 2026 — job demand rising.
Highest new-listing YoY growth (+24.5%) among smaller submarkets; buyer leverage.
Farthest commute; posted crime rate is a small-town artifact of the FBI aggregation — treat cautiously.

submarkets.invalidation: Fails your 20-min commute rule and sits closest to a fresh WARN filing. Only revisit if BMW opens Woodruff hiring pipeline.
submarkets.name: Duncan
notes: Tyger River Industrial Park hub; Duncan flagged as ~19% growth 'Upstate Boomtown' with lowest median ($259K).
Listings collapsed −52% YoY — the tightest submarket. Expect competition in 2027.
Saddle Creek Logistics WARN (130 jobs) is Duncan-adjacent — watch for spillover.

submarkets.invalidation: Fails commute rule and district 5 is the largest — school assignment matters more than town choice.
submarkets.name: Lyman
notes: Solid, mid-size town with the metro's best cable/fiber overlap.
Listings +9.5% YoY — modest buyer leverage growing.
Farther out; commute exceeds your 20-min rule.

submarkets.invalidation: Crime rate is inflated by the FBI's zip-vs-town geography, but do drive the neighborhood you're considering — commercial-adjacent lots feel very different from interior subdivisions.
submarkets.name: Moore
notes: Reidville Rd commercial corridor rapidly expanding — lots of new inventory.
Listings +44.9% YoY, the largest surge in the metro — most negotiating leverage.
District 6 (Dorman HS) is a strong suburban district.

submarkets.invalidation: Battery-plant proximity cuts both ways: employment upside, but also concentrated exposure if BMW's global losses lead to shift cuts.
submarkets.name: Woodruff
notes: BMW's new $700M battery plant opens December 2026 with ~300 jobs — direct proximity.
Listings +38.6% YoY = strong buyer leverage.
3 fiber providers overlap here; possibly the best homelab connectivity in the metro.

crime.note: Not directly gathered — check municipal report

submarkets.invalidation: Priced above your target and outside your commute radius. Only justified if a partner works in Greenville.
submarkets.name: Greer (NW + Central)
notes: Priciest submarket — 29650 median $409K (+13.6% YoY), 29651 $354K.
Straddles Greenville/Spartanburg counties; property-tax structure differs by side.
Fails 20-minute commute; watch Univar (99) + thyssenkrupp (110) Greer WARN filings.

submarkets.invalidation: Only 43 active listings, so you may not find the 3-bed/1400+ house you want with acceptable HOA/lot in the window. Have a backup.
submarkets.name: Roebuck
notes: Small, quiet town on I-26 south of the city — 14-minute commute passes your rule.
Inventory very thin (43 active) — hard to find the exact house, but sellers still won't get much above list (7% above-list rate).
Best fiber overlap in the metro (69% availability, 4 providers).

submarkets.invalidation: Fails commute rule; the low N in every stat here (935 residents) means all rates are noisy — walk the specific street.
submarkets.name: Chesnee
notes: Highest median PPSF in the county at $174 — 29323 pays for larger lots on the NC line.
Deepest price decline in group (−5.6% YoY).
Rural feel, low inventory (82), Chesnee-owned fiber is a rare rural bonus.
